decode: arg0=utf8
arg0 is a Riot Client run log as src/main/launchers/riot/client-log.ts reads it (readRange / readTail in src/main/launchers/log-read.ts: Buffer.toString('utf8'); a BOM stays as U+FEFF, invalid bytes become U+FFFD).
The readers cap what they hand over (readLogSince keeps the last 8 MiB and drops a clipped first line, currentRunBuild reads 512 bytes); the function relies on that and enforces only its own line cap.
Caps the function enforces: a line longer than MAX_LOG_LINE_LENGTH (16384) UTF-16 code units is skipped (cap-line-*), and a launch-declined reason is 1 to 80 UTF-16 code units ([^()]{1,80} without the u flag; cap-reason-*).
All seven fixture logs are cases (fixture-*), each as the file the bundle holds.
The regexes have no u flag: \d is ASCII, \s is JS whitespace (U+FEFF yes, U+0085 no), `.` stops at CR, LF, U+2028 and U+2029, `$` is the end of the line string, and /i folds ASCII only. The adv-* cases aim at each difference from Rust regex defaults.

regex: lines ended by CR CR LF: the split leaves a CR at the end, the JS `.` of the prefix pattern stops there and `$` cannot match, so every line is dropped; a Rust `.` takes the CR
regex: two client lines joined by a lone CR: one line to the split, which the JS prefix pattern refuses at the CR
regex: U+2028 and U+2029 inside a line: JS `.` does not match them, so the line is dropped; Rust `.` does
unicode-digit: the timestamp in Arabic-Indic digits and fullwidth digits: JS \d refuses both
unicode-digit: a build number in Arabic-Indic digits, and an rso-auth status of Devanagari digits: JS \d refuses them
word-boundary: a build followed by é: JS \b is ASCII, so it falls after the last digit and the build is 140.0.6.5027; a Unicode \b sees é as a word character and backs off to 140.0.6
unicode-space: U+FEFF where the patterns allow \s: before the level, after a PSL state, before a launch argument; JS \s matches U+FEFF, Rust \s does not
unicode-space: U+0085 where the patterns allow \s: JS \s does not match it, Rust \s does
unicode-space: U+00A0 and U+3000 where the patterns allow \s: both JS and Unicode \s match them
case-mapping: ids with U+017F (long s) and U+212A (Kelvin) under /i: JS without the u flag folds ASCII only and refuses them; Rust (?i) folds them to s and k
case-mapping: an id with U+0130 (dotted capital I) under /i: refused by JS; toLowerCase would turn it into two code units
utf8-decode: invalid bytes in a PSL state, a product id and a settings key; each maximal invalid subsequence becomes one U+FFFD and the patterns refuse the line
utf8-decode: an invalid byte in the user name of a settings-written line: \S matches U+FFFD, so the event stands
